findings.F1: The book's loss comes from its shorts. Short positions summed −10.46 of daily position gain, against +1.16 for longs. The 2189 short trades lost 5.95 % each on average after fees, while the 1638 long trades gained 1.96 %.
findings.F2: The combined score points the wrong way inside the 90-day rise. Its rank correlation with the next 5-day unusual move is −0.055 (p 0.023, 1704 cases). The 57 % of cases where it was short were followed by +0.85 % (t 2.14), and the cases where it was long by −0.73 % (t −1.80). That is why the idea's size is −0.43 % per case, 2.2 times the 0.19 % cost and of the wrong sign.
findings.F3: The relearned weights give two components the opposite sign to what they predict in a rise.
findings.F4: The weights do not carry forward from one period to the next. By year, the score's correlation with the 28-day return swings from −0.46 to +0.48, and its correlation with the move is negative in 7 of 8 years (−0.06 to −0.31).
findings.F5: The 28-day return alone does predict the move in a 90-day rise (rank correlation +0.081, p 0.004, 1272 cases).
findings.F6: In a 90-day rise, coins farthest from their 90-day high were followed by −1.22 % (t −1.74). Coins in the upper three fifths of closeness were followed by +1.02 % to +1.21 %.
findings.F7: When the combined score disagreed in sign with the 28-day return (696 cases, 77 % of them short), its bets earned −1.26 % per case. When they agreed (576 cases), they earned +0.55 %.
findings.F8: Outside a 90-day rise, the relation reverses. The 28-day return (−0.065, p 0.025) and closeness to the 90-day high (−0.074, p 0.007) both point to lower next 5-day returns.

ideas.idea: While a coin's 90-day return is positive, the higher its 28-day return, the larger its rise over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: In a coin's 90-day rise, a trader leans long harder the stronger its 28-day climb, and refuses shorts the combined score would have taken against that climb.
ideas.name: monthly momentum inside uptrends

ideas.idea: While a coin's 90-day return is positive, the closer its close is to its 90-day closing high, the larger its rise over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: Inside a 90-day rise, a coin near its high is a reason to be long, and one far below it a reason to stay out.
ideas.name: nearness to high in uptrends

ideas.idea: A coin's return over the next 5 days lines up more closely with its relearned combined score of its 28-day return, last 1-day return, closeness to its 90-day high and 30-day volatility than with the score of whichever single signal has predicted best, only while its 90-day return is positive and the combined score points the same way as its 28-day return, and the more positive that 90-day return the closer the fit.
ideas.consequence: A trader takes the combined score's bets only when they follow the coin's 28-day direction, which drops the shorts that carried the book's loss.
ideas.name: combination agreeing with momentum

ideas.idea: While a coin's 90-day return is not positive, the higher its 28-day return, the lower its return over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: Outside a 90-day rise, a strong 28-day bounce is a reason to expect a fall, not to join it.
ideas.name: momentum reverses in downtrends
